properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud 2026-08-08, immediately after `dec:an-unplanned-cut-slips-every-later-increment-by-one` was accepted and applied, and in direct response to the id-churn cost that applying it exposed. HIS WORDS: "if we can't slip a version, just add the in-between version like v0.25.1 for the planned change, then preplanned versions can stay in place (their id stays the same) and we can add unplanned versions as v0.25.1 or v0.26.4 or whatever makes sense - I'm sure this has a drawback also as it probably doesn't fit when you should do a minor bump versus whatever the third decimal place is called." (The third decimal is the PATCH number, semver's MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.) THE IDEA: an unplanned cut is numbered BETWEEN the planned ones rather than consuming one of them, so `epoch:v0260-planned` stays v0.26.0 forever, its id keeps matching its content, and nothing renumbers. WHAT IT SOLVES, and it is the real prize: the id churn is not merely reduced, it is ELIMINATED — no renaming, no risk to the snapshot history `dec:arrival-delta` reads plan movement from, and no ids that lie about their content. It also removes the cascade entirely: today's slip touched four epochs, and a scheme where planned numbers are stable touches none. THE DRAWBACK HE NAMED HIMSELF, AND IT IS REAL AND MEASURABLE ON TODAY'S CUT: patch is not a free slot. This project's CHANGELOG defines its own buckets — patch is "bug fixes, doc fixes, tests, refactors, perf, and behavior changes that make a silent failure LOUD", minor is "a change to the SHAPE of the tool surface (new/changed params, changed result shapes)". v0.25.0 was MINOR by that table for exactly two reasons: `HealProposal.would_destroy` and `HealIssue.hubs`, both new result fields. Everything else in it was fixes. So v0.25.1 would have been WRONG for what actually shipped — by a hair, and the hair matters. THE HARM IS CONCRETE RATHER THAN PURIST, and the same table states it: patch means the consumer "updates blindly; skills and calls unchanged"; minor means they "may need to notice". Numbering a shape change as a patch tells Alex he can update without looking when a result shape moved. That is a signal saying SAFE without having checked — the failure family this whole session kept finding. OTHER SHAPES, none chosen: (a) HYBRID — insert as a patch when the unplanned work genuinely IS a patch (the common case), slip only when it is genuinely minor (rarer). Keeps ids stable most of the time and keeps semver honest; costs two rules instead of one and a judgement at each cut, though that judgement is one the CHANGELOG table already forces. (b) DISSOLVE IT — name planned increments by CONTENT and assign the number at cut time from what actually shipped (`dec:idea-a-planned-increment-is-named-by-content-not-by-number`). Then neither slipping nor inserting is a problem, because no plan ever holds a number it can lose. This is the only option where the question stops existing rather than being answered. (c) REDEFINE THE BUCKETS — pre-1.0 semver gives latitude and the project has not made a stability commitment ("Major 1.0 — Deferred"), so it could declare that 0.x.y patch admits additive-but-non-breaking changes. Cheapest to write and the most expensive to be wrong about, since it weakens the one signal consumers act on blindly. (d) KEEP THE ACCEPTED RULE and pay the id cost, treating ids as birth numbers rather than delivery numbers. WORTH NOTING: (a) and (b) COMPOSE — content-named plans plus semver-honest numbering at cut time is arguably the same answer reached from two directions.
properties.name: OPEN — should unplanned work take an IN-BETWEEN version (v0.25.1) so planned increments never renumber, instead of slipping them all up one?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an idea rather than as a change because Anthony was explicitly thinking out loud, offered the counter-argument himself in the same breath, and the accepted rule it revisits was settled minutes earlier. Nothing is superseded: `dec:an-unplanned-cut-slips-every-later-increment-by-one` stands and the slip has been applied. What makes this worth a node rather than a passing remark is that it is a genuine alternative to a rule with a known cost, and the cost is what prompted it — so a later session choosing between them needs both on the record, with the semver objection attached to the idea rather than lost in conversation.
